clue.text: Detectives catching person unknown returned with great energy

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled string is sent back the way it came, read right to left
catching means the detectives' letters close round and hold the person unknown

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives
a man is a person
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: Police detectives are said to have arrested a mystery man and come back full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' and 'returned' work in turn: the detectives hold the unknown person first, and only then is the whole lot turned round. 'person unknown' is two pieces, not one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dynamic is forceful and vigorous, full of drive and energy.

clue.text: Evolutionist's prominent place in NT

definitions.meaning: Charles ... proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection
The capital city of Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the evolutionary naturalist and to the capital of the Northern Territory.

clue.text: Issue marking the end of Gordon Brown

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of Gordon

parts.note: umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A newspaper edition reporting the fall of the former prime minister Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a British prime minister; here 'Brown' is just a colour, UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a magazine is a number, as in the latest number.

clue.text: Psychic fills pitman with awe

indicators.note: fills means the awe goes inside the pitman like a filling

parts.note: a pitman is a coal miner
dread is a feeling of awe and fear

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant strikes terror into a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills' asks for the awe to go inside the pitman; a pitman is an old word for a coal-mine worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader claims to know others' thoughts, a kind of psychic.

clue.text: International artist, creator of great pictures

parts.note: an international player wins a cap for playing for their country
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter of world renown who produced magnificent canvases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pictures' are motion pictures: Frank Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra was a Hollywood film director, a maker of great motion pictures.

clue.text: Soldier's weapon against indigestion

parts.note: a soldier is a caste of ant, here with a possessive that leads into its weapon
acid (formic acid) is the weapon an ant sprays or stings with

explanation.surface: A soldier's arms, oddly enough, turn out to be a remedy for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is not a person but a soldier ant, whose weapon is acid: the surface sense of 'weapon' as a rifle misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective an antacid medicine counteracts stomach acidity, so it works against indigestion.

clue.text: One who could make name among Greek royalty

indicators.note: could make means the letters given can be formed into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone able to win fame among the Greek kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who could make' signals rearranging NAME AMONG; 'One who' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Vessel passing over a fish

indicators.note: passing over means, in a down entry, the vessel sits above the a

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A boat sails over a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a boat but is a cask, TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large sea fish.

clue.text: Some of them worked in Hackney to train players

definitions.text: Some of them worked in Hackney

parts.note: to coach is to train
men are players in a team

explanation.surface: Locals in a London borough coach the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but a hackney is a horse-drawn hire carriage, driven by coachmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Coachmen drove hackney carriages, horse-drawn cabs for hire, so some worked in a hackney.

clue.text: Moulds chance events

definitions.meaning: objects shaped in a metal mould, and to die-cast is to mould
a die cast, a throw of the dice, is a matter of chance

explanation.definitionFit: Die-casts are metal objects made in moulds, and casts of a die are pure chance.

clue.text: Upright type in novel

definitions.meaning: the ordinary upright typeface, as opposed to italic
... is the French word for a novel, also used in English for a type of novel such as ... à clef

explanation.definitionFit: Roman names the upright style of print and, borrowed from French, a novel.

clue.text: No oil painting line Japan developed

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters being worked up into a new form, like film being processed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Japanese line drawing that came out of the developing tray is clearly not an oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges LINE and JAPAN. 'No oil painting' is the British idiom for someone unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain Jane is an unattractive woman; calling someone no oil painting is the same British put-down.

clue.text: Chill first of Riesling in large vessel — that will get party going

parts.note: ice chills drinks, and to ice is to chill

indicators.note: in means the Riesling's opening letter goes inside the large vessel

parts.note: a beaker is a large drinking cup or vessel

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the wine's name

explanation.surface: Put some Riesling on ice in a big jug and the party will warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the Riesling's R inside the large vessel, giving BEARKER; the hyphenated answer is a party game or opening remark, not a ship here.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is an activity or remark that relaxes people and gets a gathering going.

clue.text: Article on a girl

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces: THE placed with A. 'Article' looks like a piece of writing but is the grammatical word THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea is a girl's given name, the crossword's usual sense of girl.

clue.text: One puts one's heart into playing dual role getting runs

indicators.note: into means the heart goes inside the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters being played about with into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letter of one

explanation.surface: A performer commits fully to a two-sided part and is rewarded with runs.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the heart of 'one', goes into ALLROUDE (from 'dual role', rearranged) plus R. An all-rounder in cricket both bats and bowls, so plays a dual role.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is just 'One', which an all-rounder is: a player who is one of the team.

clue.text: Lib annotated sorting out the deficit

indicators.note: sorting out suggests the letters being put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician marks up papers while tackling the budget shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' rearranges LIB and ANNOTATED; 'Lib' is short for a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's national debt is the total it owes, the accumulated deficit of the government.

clue.text: Dyed-in-the-wool Grannie and I'd wrangle

indicators.note: wrangle suggests arguing and twisting things round, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Grandmother and I always argue, and nothing will change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrangle' rearranges GRANNIE and I'D; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed in the wool means fixed and deep-rooted, just as an ingrained habit is.

clue.text: Parson mostly cut humorous verse

indicators.note: mostly means the parson word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cleric is a clergyman such as a parson
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A vicar mostly snipped out a comic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the parson's final letter. The clerihew is named after its inventor, Edmund Clerihew Bentley.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line biographical verse, a kind of humorous poem.

clue.text: English got to bottom of rifle securing a volley of shots

indicators.note: securing means the shifted rifle name holds the a inside it
got to bottom of means the English letter travels down to the foot of the rifle's name in this down entry

parts.note: the Lee-Enfield was the standard British army rifle

explanation.surface: An Englishman reached the base of his rifle while firing off a burst of shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of ENFIELD (the English) drops to the bottom, ENFILDE, and A goes inside: ENFIL-A-DE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enfilade is a volley of gunfire raking along a line of troops from end to end.

clue.text: Rich countrymen used parachute perhaps swapping sides near the end

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so swapping them changes the L near the end of the phrase into an R

parts.note: a parachutist comes down softly, so has landed gently

explanation.surface: Wealthy country folk dropped in by parachute.
explanation.walkthrough: Left (L) becomes right (R) in the second word only, the one 'near the end'. Landed gentry are British landowning families living on country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed gentry are wealthy owners of country estates, rich people of the countryside.

clue.text: Start diamond business

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Launching a jewellery firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like a verb but is the noun OFF, as in from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place of business, and also a duty or function.

clue.text: Painter hampered by parking restrictions

indicators.note: hampered by means the answer is held in, boxed in, by the words that follow

explanation.surface: An artist finds his work slowed by rules about where he can leave his car.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'parkING RESTrictions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter.

clue.text: Track bird

definitions.meaning: a track on which trains or curtains run
a ... is a marsh bird such as the water ...

explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a running bar or railway line and also a wading marsh bird.

clue.text: Urchin gets a cake after scrap

indicators.note: after means the a and the cake follow the scrap in the answer

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A street kid is handed a little cake following a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but is a rag, a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child, the same as a street urchin.

clue.text: Match occupying most of a grassed area

indicators.note: most of means the grassed area word loses its last letter

parts.note: a green is a grassed area, such as a village green

explanation.surface: A football game held on part of the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a game, but it is the verb meaning to correspond; 'most of' trims the grassed area, and 'occupying' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to agree, to correspond or tally with something.

clue.text: Escape making a pound in payment

indicators.note: in means the pound goes inside the payment

parts.note: a fee is a payment
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Get away with a pound as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: L sits inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, to escape.

clue.text: Captain ship, one making the news

parts.note: a head is a leader or chief, as a captain is
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: The captain of an ocean liner gets into the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as one who makes the headlines, the top story.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the star attraction, the person whose name tops the bill and the headlines.

clue.text: More restrained fan

definitions.meaning: the comparative of dry in the sense of restrained or understated, as in dry humour
a blower or fan used to dry hair or clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Drier means more understated, and a drier is also a hot-air blower such as a hairdryer.

clue.text: When one has spare time do some gardening, keeping within range

indicators.note: keeping within means the gardening word holds the range inside it

parts.note: to weed is a gardening job
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Someone with free time potters in the garden while staying close to home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping within' has the gardening job hold the range; 'range' is ken, knowledge, as in beyond my ken.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekend, Saturday and Sunday, is when most people are free from work.

clue.text: Like Van Gogh, producing French art around his work place

indicators.note: around means the French verb form wraps round the painter's town

parts.note: es is French for (thou) art, from the verb to be
Van Gogh painted many of his best-known works in Arles in Provence

explanation.surface: A French artist's studio is linked to a painter famous for his ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old English 'are', not painting; Van Gogh cut off part of his ear while living at Arles.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh famously severed part of his ear, so he could be described as lacking one.
